findings.title: The VERDICT_STRICT bash guard reads '>' and '<' inside quoted strings and heredoc bodies as output redirection and resolves the phantom target against the checkout, blocking read-only QA commands
evidence: UNTOUCHED IN THIS RANGE: `git log --oneline 32d1c41..HEAD -- hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py` is empty. The mechanism is unchanged since it was filed.

RE-PROVEN THREE MORE TIMES THIS SESSION, on three read-only commands, with the checkout unmodified throughout. (1) `rm -rf $SC` where $SC was a shell variable holding a scratchpad path - refused with "rm targets '$SC (unresolved $variable - use a literal path)'". That one is arguably correct behaviour and is recorded as the guard's honest half. (2) A `<<'PY'` heredoc whose Python body contained the f-string `f"          -> {test...}"` - refused with "output redirection targets '<checkout>/{test.split('::')[-1]}:'". (3) `git log --format=fuller`-adjacent: `git log --format='%H%n%an <%ae>%n...'` - refused with "output redirection targets '<checkout>/%n%(trailers)%n---''", from a `<` inside a single-quoted argument.

NEW INFORMATION FROM CASE (3): the previous reproductions were all about '>'. This one is '<', inside single quotes, in a git format string - so the scan treats both redirection operators the same way and quoting is invisible to it in both directions. Case (2) confirms run 5's finding that heredoc framing is also invisible.

The blocked constructs are ordinary in the material a tester must read: '->' is a Python return annotation appearing on 100+ lines of this repository's own source, and '<...>' is the shape of every email address in a git author field.

COST, measured: three retries this session, each costing one round trip and a reworded command. No finding was lost - I reformulated each command and got the evidence - which is why this stays Minor. It would rise to Major if a project's only route to a piece of evidence went through a blocked shape.
unchanged by this range: `git diff --name-only 7357bfc..1ae041c -- hooks/` prints nothing

re-demonstrated five times in this session, every time on a read-only QA probe that wrote nothing anywhere. A heredoc whose Python body contained the ASCII arrow '->' inside a quoted print string was refused with "output redirection targets '.../verdict-clone/\", (a git checkout under /private/tmp)'"; the phantom target was the text following the arrow. The same happened on a body containing the comparison `_num(came_back) > _num(prior.get(...))`, and on the evidence line you are reading, which had to be built with chr(62) to be written at all

two further shapes of the same family cost a command each: a relative redirect target after a `cd` into the scratch directory is resolved against the session cwd (the checkout) rather than the directory just cd'd into, and a $VAR target is refused outright ('unresolved $variable - use a literal path')

findings.title: The strict bash guard treats every non-flag argument of cp/mv/rsync as a write target, so copying the checkout into a scratch temp dir - the re-injection step the agent contract mandates - is refused in the same words as overwriting the checkout
evidence: hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:38-42 declares _MUTATORS as 'commands whose non-flag arguments name files they (may) mutate', and hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:354-357 yields every non-flag argument as a candidate target, the source included

probe feeding the hook its own PreToolUse payload with VERDICT_STRICT=1: `cp -a [checkout] [scratch]/tree2` exits 2 DENIED, and `cp -a [scratch]/x.py [checkout]/src/verdict_mcp/harness.py` exits 2 DENIED with the same message. The guard cannot tell the two apart and reports the read-only copy as targeting the checkout

the identical read-only copy expressed as `python3 -c 'import shutil; shutil.copytree(...)'` exits 0 allowed, which is the guard's documented design (hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:10-17, 'Unknown commands are ALLOWED', 'this is a deny-HEURISTIC, not a sandbox'). The denial therefore costs a workflow and adds no protection: it moves the same operation to an unchecked interpreter

cost, live: this run needed a scratch copy of the tree to re-inject four defects, which agents/verdict.md sections 3.5 and 6 require ('in a scratch copy of the tree (never the checkout)'), and the first attempt was refused

root_cause.symptom: a read-only copy out of the checkout is denied as though it wrote to the checkout
root_cause.mechanism: the _MUTATORS fallback arm at hooks/enforce_bash_scope.py:354 yields all non-flag arguments with no positional semantics, so argv[0] of a cp is treated as a destination
root_cause.origin: the fallback arm predates this range - `git diff --name-only 7357bfc..1ae041c -- hooks/` prints nothing - and this is the first run that needed a whole-tree copy for re-injection
root_cause.class: searched `grep -rn '_MUTATORS' hooks/*.py`: four uses, three of them dedicated position-aware checkers (tar at :350, find at :352, stream editors at :237) and one positional-blind fallback at :354. cp, mv, rsync, install and ln all reach the blind arm, so every source-to-destination command in the set carries the same false positive

proof.detail: both directions of the same cp are denied identically while the python equivalent is allowed

root_cause.latent_condition: the guard has per-command checkers for tar and find but none for the source/destination commands, and no test asserts that a legitimate copy out of the checkout is permitted

.qa/profile.md:7 front matter carries coverage_suite_cmd (`uv run --group dev python -m coverage run -m pytest tests/ -q -o addopts=`), and this run measured 122 of 143 changed lines with it

root_cause.mechanism: the prose was written at baseline and not revisited when the coverage pipeline and its front-matter key arrived; nothing cross-checks prose against the front matter or against pyproject
